info.title: TESDA-TRACK API
info.description: Training and assessment pathway recommendations backed by PostgreSQL.

schema.title: Response List Qualifications Api V1 Qualifications Get

post.description:
Qualifications to suggest from a learner profile alone, for the TSP webview's entry page.

Nothing is typed here: the profile comes from the TSP launch hints and the learner's Skill Passport, so the
suggestions are worked out from those and `basis` says which of them were used. Like the rest of analysis,
the profile is neither stored nor logged.

404.description: Suggestions are turned off on this server (TSP_SUGGESTIONS_ENABLED)

post.description:
A learner's answer to "Are you satisfied with this recommendation?", signed in or not.

The API works the matches and readiness result out again from what the finder sent, and keeps the answer with
those numbers and the matching model's name. The goal is kept only as a keyed hash, and the answer isn't linked
to an account.

429.description: Too many answers from this client; see Retry-After

patch.description:
Why the learner wasn't satisfied, given after an answer of No; after "wrong_qualification", optionally the
qualification they wanted instead.

404.description: No such answer, or no such wanted qualification

429.description: Too many answers from this client; see Retry-After

post.description:
The goal's words, which the learner agreed to share to test and train matching, labelled with the qualification
their answer says fits. Kept apart from the answer and the account; the pilot team reviews them before any use.

409.description: An answer of No without the qualification the learner wanted

422.description: Not the goal the answer was about, or no consent

429.description: Too many answers from this client; see Retry-After

post.description: Verified, available, eligible schedules with seats; no embedding model is required.
Structured matching works on a CPU without invoking an embedding model or storing guest answers.

Training programs for a qualification, ranked by the weighted score with each component shown.

Works without signing in; a signed-in learner's rankings are linked to their account in the audit trail.

A personalized report on the chosen qualification's pathway: options, units to work on, why, and next steps.

Worked out again from what the finder sent, as feedback is, with deterministic templates over the matching,
readiness, the two rankings above (audited as usual; their audit ids are in `rankings`) and, signed in, the
learner's own records. The goal is neither stored nor repeated; a region only sorts options by distance.

Positive feedback by qualification, saved-session learner demand, and model/rules review priorities.

Projections use two complete 30-day windows and sample/history gates. They are trend estimates,

Per qualification: how often it was the top match or chosen, readiness, and assessment outcomes.

Read external matches for explicitly supplied skill terms. Only the terms are sent; responses are cached

Find occupations by title; capability terms continue through ``/matches``.

get.description: Qualifications, a bounded skills preview, and existing benchmark mappings for a public occupation id.

post.description:
Skills Explorer in one request: extract skill and role terms from a short sentence, search title terms as
occupations and the rest as skills, and return both together.

Only the extracted terms go to Skills Bridge; the text itself is not logged, cached or sent. Each of the (at
most two) lookups runs through the same limits and cache as ``/occupations/search`` and ``/matches``, so it
counts against the per-client limit like a call to those endpoints. Text with no usable terms returns
``searched: false`` and a ``reason`` without contacting Skills Bridge or using the limit.
Bounded, atomic upsert of reviewed evidence. Dry runs validate and roll back all writes.

put.description: Replace reviewed source evidence. Training and assessment authorization are independent.

patch.description: Replace answers in a new immutable revision; historical results keep the original reference.

get.description:
Directions from the learner's location to a center: a road route for each travel mode the router has (car,
bike and foot from the public router; car only from a self-hosted one), then an estimated flight for a long
trip. No sign-in needed.

The origin is rounded to about a kilometre before it's used, cached or sent to the router, and isn't logged.
When this server has no router (ROUTING_URL empty), the answer is `routing_enabled: false` with no routes:
link to Google Maps instead.

schema.title: Response Public Indicators Api V1 Labor Market Indicators Get

get.description: Reviewed qualification links for an area; observations and forecasts stay separate.

One qualification across the regions: posting records beside the recorded training and assessment centers,
each region's balance of the two, and the analysis of `region_code` in plain words. `home_region_code` is the
learner's own region and `relocate` whether they would move; both only change the wording. No sign-in needed,
and no learner input or coordinates are read.

The outlook's analysis as one short paragraph. `source` is "ai" when Claude wrote it from the counts
(OUTLOOK_AI_SUMMARY_ENABLED), and "rules" when AI summaries are off, busy or unavailable: the same analysis in
the rules' own words.

post.description:
Compare up to eight known qualification sites using the chosen road mode.

The departure point stays in the POST body, is rounded to two decimal places before cache/network use,
and is not persisted in a ranking audit. Site coordinates are resolved from the catalog, not the body.
Route evidence does not establish authority, availability or learner eligibility.

429.description: Too many comparison requests from this client
